Volume of a prism = Base Area × Height

Base is an equilateral triangle with side a = 15 cm.

Base Area = (√3/4) × a2 = (√3/4) × 152 = 225√3/4 cm2

Volume = (225√3/4) × 20√3 = 225 × 5 × (√3 × √3) = 225 × 5 × 3

Volume = 225 × 15 = 3375 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 3375 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of equilateral triangular base (a) = 15 cm

Height of the prism (h) = 20√3 cm

Formula Used:

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3/4) × side2

Volume of Prism = Base Area × Height

Calculations:

⇒ Area of the base = (√3/4) × (15)2

⇒ Area of the base = (√3/4) × 225 cm2

⇒ Volume of the prism = [(√3/4) × 225] × 20√3

⇒ Volume = (225 × 20 × √3 × √3) ÷ 4

⇒ Volume = (225 × 20 × 3) ÷ 4

⇒ Volume = 225 × 5 × 3

⇒ Volume = 225 × 15

⇒ Volume = 3375 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 3375 cm3.

Additional Information

Lateral Surface Area (LSA) of Prism

LSA = Perimeter of base × Height of the prism. For this prism, LSA = (3 × 15) × 20√3 = 900√3 cm2.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Prism

TSA = Lateral Surface Area + 2 × Area of base. TSA = (Perimeter × h) + 2 × [(√3/4) × a2].

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of a pyramid is exactly 1/3 the volume of a prism with the same base and height: Volume = (1/3) × Base Area × Height.

questions.question: A cone of height 45 cm is cut at a height of 15 cm from its base by a plane parallel to its base. If the volume of the smaller cone is 18480 cm 3 , then what is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the original cone?
questions.questionHtml: A cone of height 45 cm is cut at a height of 15 cm from its base by a plane parallel to its base. If the volume of the smaller cone is 18480 cm<sup>3</sup>, then what is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the original cone?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Height of original cone (H) = 45 cm; Height of smaller cone (h) = 45 − 15 = 30 cm.

Ratio of heights (Small : Large) = 30 : 45 = 2 : 3.

Ratio of volumes = (Height ratio)3 = 23 : 33 = 8 : 27.

Given, 8 units = 18480 cm3 ⇒ 1 unit = 2310 cm3.

Volume of original cone = 27 units = 27 × 2310 = 62370 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 62370 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Height (H) = 45 cm

Cutting Height from base = 15 cm

Volume of smaller cone (v) = 18480 cm3

Formula Used:

Ratio of volumes of two similar cones = (Ratio of their heights)3

Calculations:

⇒ Height of smaller cone (h) = 45 − 15 = 30 cm

⇒ Ratio of heights (k) = h ÷ H = 30 ÷ 45 = 2/3

⇒ Volume of small cone ÷ Volume of large cone = (h/H)3

⇒ 18480 ÷ V = (2/3)3

⇒ 18480 ÷ V = 8/27

⇒ V = (18480 × 27) ÷ 8

⇒ V = 2310 × 27

⇒ V = 62370 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 62370 cm3.

Additional Information

Volume of Frustum

The volume of the bottom part remaining after the cut (frustum) is Vfrustum = (1/3)πh(R2 + r2 + Rr), or simply Vlarge − Vsmall.

Similarity Property of Solids

For any two similar 3D figures, the ratio of their volumes is the cube of the ratio of any corresponding linear dimensions (height, radius, or slant height).

Surface Area Ratio

The ratio of the curved surface areas of the smaller cone to the original cone is (h/H)2. In this case, (2/3)2 = 4/9.

questions.question: The ratio of the curved surface area and total surface area of a right circular cylinder is 2 : 5. If the total surface area is 3080 cm 2 , then what is the volume (in cm 3 ) of the cylinder?
questions.questionHtml: The ratio of the curved surface area and total surface area of a right circular cylinder is 2 : 5. If the total surface area is 3080 cm<sup>2</sup>, then what is the volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of CSA : TSA = h : (h + r) = 2 : 5 → h = 2 units, r = 3 units.

Since TSA is 5 units = 3080 cm2, then CSA (2πrh) = 2 units = 1232 cm2.

Area of two bases (2πr2) = TSA − CSA = 3080 − 1232 = 1848 cm2.

πr2 = 924 ⇒ r2 = 294 ⇒ r = 7√6 cm and h = (2/3)r = 14√6 / 3 cm.

Volume = πr2h = 924 × (14√6 / 3) = 4312√6 cm3.

∴ The correct answer is 4312√6 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total Surface Area (TSA) of cylinder = 3080 cm2

Ratio of Curved Surface Area (CSA) to TSA = 2 : 5

Formula Used:

CSA = 2πrh

TSA = 2πr(h + r)

Volume (V) = πr2h

Calculations:

⇒ CSA / TSA = (2πrh) / [2πr(h + r)] = 2 / 5

⇒ h / (h + r) = 2 / 5

⇒ 5h = 2h + 2r

⇒ 3h = 2r ⇒ h = 2r / 3

⇒ CSA = (2/5) × TSA = (2/5) × 3080 = 1232 cm2

⇒ TSA − CSA = Area of 2 circular bases = 3080 − 1232 = 1848 cm2

⇒ 2πr2 = 1848

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r2 = 1848

⇒ r2 = (1848 × 7) / 44 = 42 × 7 = 294

⇒ r = √294 = 7√6 cm

⇒ h = (2/3) × 7√6 = 14√6 / 3 cm

⇒ Volume = πr2h = (22/7) × 294 × (14√6 / 3)

⇒ Volume = 924 × (14√6 / 3)

⇒ Volume = 308 × 14√6 = 4312√6 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 4312√6 cm3.

Additional Information

Cylinder Surface Areas

The lateral surface area is 2πrh, and the total surface area includes the top and bottom circles: 2πrh + 2πr2.

Volume Comparison

A cylinder has 3 times the volume of a cone with the same radius and height: Vcylinder = 3 × Vcone = πr2h.

Hollow Cylinder

For a hollow cylinder with outer radius R and inner radius r, Volume = πh(R2 − r2).

questions.question: The radius and height of a solid cylinder are increased by 2% each. What will be the approximate percentage increase in volume?
questions.questionHtml: The radius and height of a solid cylinder are increased by 2% each. What will be the approximate percentage increase in volume?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Volume of cylinder depends on r2 and h (V ∝ r × r × h).

Successive % increase of 2% and 2% = 2 + 2 + (2 × 2)/100 = 4.04%.

Successive % increase of 4.04% and 2% = 4.04 + 2 + (4.04 × 2)/100 = 6.04 + 0.0808 = 6.1208%.

Approximate increase ≈ 6.12%.

∴ The correct answer is 6.12%.

Alternate Method

Given: Increase in radius (r) = 2%, Increase in height (h) = 2%.

Formula Used: Volume of cylinder (V) = πr2h

⇒ Let original radius (r) = 100 and original height (h) = 100.

⇒ Original Volume (V1) = π × (100)2 × 100 = 1,000,000π.

⇒ New radius (r') = 100 + 2% of 100 = 102.

⇒ New height (h') = 100 + 2% of 100 = 102.

⇒ New Volume (V2) = π × (102)2 × 102 = π × 10404 × 102 = 1,061,208π.

⇒ Increase in Volume = V2 − V1 = 1,061,208π − 1,000,000π = 61,208π.

⇒ Percentage Increase = (61,208π / 1,000,000π) × 100 = 6.1208%.

⇒ Approximate Percentage Increase ≈ 6.12%.

∴ The correct answer is 6.12%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage for 3 Variables

For three successive changes a%, b%, and c%, the net change is given by [a + b + c + (ab + bc + ca)/100 + (abc)/10000]%.

Curved Surface Area (CSA) Change

CSA of cylinder = 2πrh. If r and h both increase by x%, the net increase in CSA is (x + x + x2/100)%.

Small Change Approximation

If a quantity depends on xayb and variables change by very small %, the net change is approximately (a × %change in x + b × %change in y).

questions.question: A sphere of radius 21 cm is cut into 8 identical parts by 3 cuts (1 cut along each axis). What will be the total surface area (in cm 2 ) of each part?
questions.questionHtml: A sphere of radius 21 cm is cut into 8 identical parts by 3 cuts (1 cut along each axis). What will be the total surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of each part?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Each octant (1/8th part) has 1/8th of the sphere's curved area and 3 flat quadrant faces.

TSA of 1 part = (1/8 × 4πr2) + (3 × 1/4πr2) = 1.25 × πr2.

Direct Calculation: 1.25 × (22/7) × 21 × 21.

TSA = 1.25 × 1386 = 1732.5 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 1732.5 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of sphere (r) = 21 cm

Sphere is cut into 8 identical parts by 3 perpendicular cuts passing through the center.

Formula Used:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of sphere = 4πr2

Total Surface Area (TSA) of each part = (1/8 × CSA of sphere) + Area of 3 flat surfaces

Area of each flat surface = Quarter of a circle = (1/4)πr2

Calculations:

⇒ Area of 1/8th curved surface = (1/8) × 4 × (22/7) × 21 × 21

⇒ Area of 1/8th curved surface = (1/2) × 22 × 3 × 21 = 11 × 63 = 693 cm2

⇒ Area of 3 flat faces = 3 × (1/4) × (22/7) × 21 × 21

⇒ Area of 3 flat faces = (3/4) × 22 × 3 × 21 = (3/2) × 11 × 63 = 2079 / 2 = 1039.5 cm2

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = 693 + 1039.5

⇒ TSA = 1732.5 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 1732.5 cm2.

Additional Information

Surface Area of Sphere and Parts

Total Surface Area of a sphere is 4πr2. When cut into two hemispheres, the TSA of one hemisphere becomes 3πr2 (curved surface 2πr2 + flat base πr2).

Effect of Cuts through Center

Each full circular cut through the center of a sphere adds an additional surface area equal to 2 × (πr2). Three perpendicular cuts create 3 full circular cross-sections, adding 6πr2 to the original 4πr2.

Volume of Sphere Parts

Volume of a full sphere is (4/3)πr3. When cut into 8 identical parts, the volume of each part is simply 1/8 of the total: V = (1/6)πr3.

questions.question: Two identical hemispheres of maximum possible size are cut from a solid cube of side 14 cm. The bases of the hemispheres are part of the two opposite faces of cube. What is the total volume (in cm 3 ) of the remaining part of the cube?
questions.questionHtml: Two identical hemispheres of maximum possible size are cut from a solid cube of side 14 cm. The bases of the hemispheres are part of the two opposite faces of cube. What is the total volume (in cm<sup>3</sup>) of the remaining part of the cube?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Side of cube (a) = 14 cm

Radius of maximum hemisphere (r) = a ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

Volume of 2 hemispheres = Volume of 1 full sphere = (4/3) × π × r3

Remaining Volume = a3 − (4/3) × (22/7) × 73 = 2744 − 1437.33 = 1306.67 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 1306.67 cm3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Side of the solid cube (a) = 14 cm

Number of hemispheres = 2 (cut from opposite faces)

Formula Used:

Volume of Cube = a3

Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r3

Calculations:

⇒ For maximum size, the diameter of each hemisphere must be equal to the side of the cube.

⇒ Diameter = 14 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of the cube = a3 = 14 × 14 × 14 = 2744 cm3

⇒ Volume of one hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r3

⇒ Volume of two hemispheres = 2 × (2/3) × (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 7

⇒ Volume of two hemispheres = (4/3) × 22 × 49 = 4312 ÷ 3 ≈ 1437.33 cm3

⇒ Remaining volume = Volume of cube − Volume of two hemispheres

⇒ Remaining volume = 2744 − 1437.33 = 1306.67 cm3

∴ The correct answer is 1306.67 cm3.

Additional Information

Volume and Surface Area of Hemisphere

Volume = (2/3)πr3, Curved Surface Area = 2πr2, and Total Surface Area = 3πr2.

Maximum Sphere in a Cube

The radius of the largest sphere that can be carved out of a cube of side 'a' is a/2.

Cube Mensuration

Volume = a3, Total Surface Area = 6a2, and Diagonal = a√3.

questions.question: Identical cubes of largest possible size are cut from a solid cuboid of size 65 cm × 26 cm × 3.9 cm. What is the total surface area (in cm 2 ) of all the small cubes taken together?
questions.questionHtml: Identical cubes of largest possible size are cut from a solid cuboid of size 65 cm × 26 cm × 3.9 cm. What is the total surface area (in cm<sup>2</sup>) of all the small cubes taken together?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Side of the largest possible cube (a) = HCF of 65, 26, and 3.9 = 1.3 cm.

Number of cubes (n) = (65 ÷ 1.3) × (26 ÷ 1.3) × (3.9 ÷ 1.3) = 50 × 20 × 3 = 3000.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of one cube = 6a2 = 6 × (1.3)2 = 6 × 1.69 = 10.14 cm2.

Total TSA of all cubes = n × TSA of one cube = 3000 × 10.14 = 30420 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 30420 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given:

Dimensions of cuboid (L, B, H) = 65 cm, 26 cm, 3.9 cm.

Formula Used:

1. Side of largest cube (a) = HCF (L, B, H)

2. Number of cubes (n) = (Volume of cuboid) ÷ (Volume of one cube)

3. Total Surface Area of n cubes = n × 6a2

Calculations:

⇒ To find HCF(65, 26, 3.9), convert all to mm: 650 mm, 260 mm, 39 mm.

⇒ 650 = 13 × 50; 260 = 13 × 20; 39 = 13 × 3.

⇒ HCF(650, 260, 39) = 13 mm = 1.3 cm.

⇒ Side of the cube (a) = 1.3 cm.

⇒ Number of cubes (n) = (65 × 26 × 3.9) ÷ (1.3 × 1.3 × 1.3)

⇒ n = (65 ÷ 1.3) × (26 ÷ 1.3) × (3.9 ÷ 1.3) = 50 × 20 × 3 = 3000.

⇒ Total Surface Area = n × 6a2 = 3000 × 6 × (1.3)2

⇒ Total Surface Area = 18000 × 1.69 = 180 × 169

⇒ Total Surface Area = 30420 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 30420 cm2.

Additional Information

HCF of Decimals

To find the HCF of decimals, multiply them by a power of 10 to make them integers, find the HCF of those integers, and then divide by the same power of 10.

Total Surface Area vs Volume

When a solid is cut into smaller pieces, the total volume remains constant, but the total surface area increases due to the creation of new exposed surfaces.

Mensuration Formulas

Volume of cuboid = L × B × H | Volume of cube = a3 | Surface area of cube = 6a2.

questions.question: A regular triangular pyramid is cut by 2 planes which are parallel to its base. The planes trisect the altitude of the pyramid. Volume of top, middle and bottom part is V 1 , V 2 and V 3 respectively. What is the value of V 1 : V 2 : V 3 ?
questions.questionHtml: A regular triangular pyramid is cut by 2 planes which are parallel to its base. The planes trisect the altitude of the pyramid. Volume of top, middle and bottom part is V<sub>1</sub>, V<sub>2</sub> and V<sub>3</sub> respectively. What is the value of V<sub>1</sub> : V<sub>2</sub> : V<sub>3</sub>?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of heights of three similar pyramids formed from the top = 1 : 2 : 3

Ratio of volumes of these nested pyramids = 13 : 23 : 33 = 1 : 8 : 27

V1 (Top part) = 1 unit

V2 (Middle part) = 8 − 1 = 7 units

V3 (Bottom part) = 27 − 8 = 19 units

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 7 : 19.

Alternate Method

Given:

Altitude of the pyramid is trisected by 2 planes parallel to the base.

Let the total height of the pyramid be H.

Heights of the three resulting pyramids (from the apex) are h, 2h, and 3h where h = H/3.

Formula Used:

For similar solids, the ratio of their volumes is the ratio of the cubes of their corresponding heights (V1/V2 = (h1/h2)3).

Calculations:

⇒ Volume of first pyramid (Top) = v1 ∝ h3

⇒ Volume of second pyramid (Top + Middle) = v2 ∝ (2h)3 = 8h3

⇒ Volume of third pyramid (Total) = v3 ∝ (3h)3 = 27h3

⇒ V1 = v1 = 1 unit (assuming h3 = 1)

⇒ V2 = v2 − v1 = 8 − 1 = 7 units

⇒ V3 = v3 − v2 = 27 − 8 = 19 units

⇒ Ratio V1 : V2 : V3 = 1 : 7 : 19

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 7 : 19.

Additional Information

Property of Similar Solids

When a solid is cut by planes parallel to the base, the smaller solids formed are similar to the original. Ratios of side/height = k, Ratios of areas = k2, Ratios of volumes = k3.

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume of any pyramid is given by V = (1/3) × Base Area × Height.

Frustum of a Pyramid

The middle and bottom parts in this question are called frustums. The volume of a frustum with base areas A1 and A2 and height h is (1/3)h(A1 + A2 + √(A1 × A2)).

questions.question: What is the value of [(cos7A + cos5A) / (sin7A – sin 5A)]?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of [(cos7A + cos5A) / (sin7A – sin 5A)]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the Sum-to-Product identities for the numerator and denominator.

Numerator: cos 7A + cos 5A = 2 cos((7A+5A)/2) cos((7A−5A)/2) = 2 cos 6A cos A.

Denominator: sin 7A − sin 5A = 2 cos((7A+5A)/2) sin((7A−5A)/2) = 2 cos 6A sin A.

Dividing Numerator by Denominator: (2 cos 6A cos A) ÷ (2 cos 6A sin A) = cos A / sin A = cot A.

∴ The correct answer is cot A.

Alternate Method

Given: Expression = [(cos 7A + cos 5A) / (sin 7A − sin 5A)]

Formula Used:

1. cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) cos((C − D)/2)

2. sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2)

Calculations:

⇒ Let C = 7A and D = 5A.

⇒ Numerator = 2 cos((7A + 5A)/2) cos((7A − 5A)/2)

⇒ Numerator = 2 cos(12A/2) cos(2A/2) = 2 cos 6A cos A

⇒ Denominator = 2 cos((7A + 5A)/2) sin((7A − 5A)/2)

⇒ Denominator = 2 cos(12A/2) sin(2A/2) = 2 cos 6A sin A

⇒ Value = [2 cos 6A cos A] / [2 cos 6A sin A]

⇒ Cancel out common term 2 cos 6A: Value = cos A / sin A

⇒ Value = cot A

∴ The correct answer is cot A.

Additional Information

Sum-to-Product Identities

sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2) and cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((D-C)/2).

Basic Trigonometric Ratios

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ and cot θ = cos θ / sin θ.

Double Angle Formulas

sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A and cos 2A = cos2A − sin2A = 2 cos2A − 1 = 1 − 2 sin2A.

questions.question: What is the value of [1 – sin (90 – 2A)] / [1 + sin (90 + 2A)]?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of [1 – sin (90 – 2A)] / [1 + sin (90 + 2A)]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use value substitution: Let A = 30°.

Expression = [1 − sin(90° − 60°)] ÷ [1 + sin(90° + 60°)]

⇒ [1 − sin 30°] ÷ [1 + sin 150°] = [1 − 0.5] ÷ [1 + 0.5]

⇒ 0.5 ÷ 1.5 = 1/3.

Check options: tan2(30°) = (1/√3)2 = 1/3.

∴ The correct answer is tan2A.

Alternate Method

Given: [1 − sin(90 − 2A)] ÷ [1 + sin(90 + 2A)]

Formula Used:

1. sin(90 − θ) = cos θ

2. sin(90 + θ) = cos θ

3. 1 − cos 2θ = 2 sin2θ

4. 1 + cos 2θ = 2 cos2θ

⇒ Numerator: 1 − sin(90 − 2A) = 1 − cos 2A

⇒ Denominator: 1 + sin(90 + 2A) = 1 + cos 2A

⇒ Expression = (1 − cos 2A) ÷ (1 + cos 2A)

⇒ Using identities: 1 − cos 2A = 2 sin2A and 1 + cos 2A = 2 cos2A

⇒ Value = (2 sin2A) ÷ (2 cos2A)

⇒ Value = sin2A ÷ cos2A = tan2A

∴ The correct answer is tan2A.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Quadrant Rules

In the first quadrant (90 − θ), all ratios are positive. In the second quadrant (90 + θ), only sine and cosecant are positive. Here, sin(90 + θ) changes to cos θ and remains positive.

Double Angle Identities

cos 2A = cos2A − sin2A = 1 − 2 sin2A = 2 cos2A − 1. These are essential for converting linear trig terms into squared terms.

Complementary Angle Formulas

sin(90 − θ) = cos θ, cos(90 − θ) = sin θ, tan(90 − θ) = cot θ.

questions.question: What is the value of sin 75° + sin 15°?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of sin 75° + sin 15°?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the Sum-to-Product formula: sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C + D) ÷ 2) cos((C − D) ÷ 2).

Here, C = 75° and D = 15°.

Sum = 2 sin((75° + 15°) ÷ 2) cos((75° − 15°) ÷ 2) = 2 sin 45° cos 30°.

Value = 2 × (1 ÷ √2) × (√3 ÷ 2) = √3 ÷ √2 = √(3/2).

∴ The correct answer is √(3/2).

Alternate Method

Given: sin 75° + sin 15°

Formula Used: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B

⇒ sin 75° = sin(45° + 30°) = sin 45° cos 30° + cos 45° sin 30°

⇒ sin 75° = (1/√2) × (√3/2) + (1/√2) × (1/2) = (√3 + 1) / (2√2)

⇒ sin 15° = sin(45° − 30°) = sin 45° cos 30° − cos 45° sin 30°

⇒ sin 15° = (1/√2) × (√3/2) − (1/√2) × (1/2) = (√3 − 1) / (2√2)

⇒ Sum = [(√3 + 1) / (2√2)] + [(√3 − 1) / (2√2)]

⇒ Sum = (√3 + 1 + √3 − 1) / (2√2) = (2√3) / (2√2) = √3 / √2

⇒ Sum = √(3/2)

∴ The correct answer is √(3/2).

Additional Information

Sum-to-Product Identities

sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C-D)/2) and sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) sin((C-D)/2).

Complementary Angles

sin θ = cos(90° − θ). Thus, sin 75° = cos 15° and sin 15° = cos 75°.

Values of 15° and 75°

sin 15° = (√3−1)/(2√2) and sin 75° = (√3+1)/(2√2). These are frequently used in competitive exams.

questions.question: What is the value of [(cos3θ + 2cos5θ + cos7θ) ÷ (cosθ + 2cos3θ + cos5θ)] + sin2θ.tan3θ?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of [(cos3θ + 2cos5θ + cos7θ) ÷ (cosθ + 2cos3θ + cos5θ)] + sin2θ.tan3θ?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Put θ = 0° in the given expression.

Value = [(cos 0° + 2 cos 0° + cos 0°) ÷ (cos 0° + 2 cos 0° + cos 0°)] + sin 0°.tan 0°

⇒ [(1 + 2(1) + 1) ÷ (1 + 2(1) + 1)] + 0 × 0 = [4 ÷ 4] + 0 = 1

Now check options for θ = 0°: (1) cos(2 × 0°) = 1, (2) sin 0° = 0, (3) tan 0° = 0.

Option 1 matches the value.

∴ The correct answer is cos2θ.

Alternate Method

Given Expression: [(cos3θ + 2cos5θ + cos7θ) ÷ (cosθ + 2cos3θ + cos5θ)] + sin2θ.tan3θ

Formula used: cos C + cos D = 2 cos[(C + D)/2] cos[(C − D)/2]

⇒ Numerator = (cos 7θ + cos 3θ) + 2 cos 5θ = 2 cos 5θ cos 2θ + 2 cos 5θ = 2 cos 5θ (cos 2θ + 1)

⇒ Denominator = (cos 5θ + cos θ) + 2 cos 3θ = 2 cos 3θ cos 2θ + 2 cos 3θ = 2 cos 3θ (cos 2θ + 1)

⇒ Fraction = [2 cos 5θ (cos 2θ + 1)] ÷ [2 cos 3θ (cos 2θ + 1)] = cos 5θ ÷ cos 3θ

⇒ Total = (cos 5θ ÷ cos 3θ) + (sin 2θ × sin 3θ ÷ cos 3θ)

⇒ Total = (cos 5θ + sin 2θ sin 3θ) ÷ cos 3θ

⇒ Total = [cos(3θ + 2θ) + sin 2θ sin 3θ] ÷ cos 3θ

⇒ Total = [cos 3θ cos 2θ − sin 3θ sin 2θ + sin 2θ sin 3θ] ÷ cos 3θ

⇒ Total = (cos 3θ cos 2θ) ÷ cos 3θ = cos 2θ

∴ The correct answer is cos2θ.

Additional Information

Sum to Product Formulas

cos C + cos D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2) and cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) sin((D−C)/2).

Compound Angle Identities

cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B and cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2θ = 2cos2θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin2θ = cos2θ − sin2θ.

Shortcut Trick

Use the substitution method by assuming θ = 0°.

Numerator = 2 sin(45° + 0°) sin(45° − 0°) = 2 sin 45° sin 45° = 2 × (1/2) = 1.

Denominator = cos(2 × 0°) = cos 0° = 1.

Expression Value = 1 ÷ 1 = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: [2sin(45° + θ) sin(45° − θ)] ÷ cos 2θ

Formula Used: 2 sin A sin B = cos(A − B) − cos(A + B)

⇒ Let A = 45° + θ and B = 45° − θ

⇒ A − B = (45° + θ) − (45° − θ) = 2θ

⇒ A + B = (45° + θ) + (45° − θ) = 90°

⇒ Numerator = cos(2θ) − cos(90°)

⇒ Numerator = cos 2θ − 0 = cos 2θ

⇒ Expression = cos 2θ ÷ cos 2θ = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

Product to Sum Identities

Key conversions: 2 sin A sin B = cos(A−B) − cos(A+B) and 2 cos A cos B = cos(A+B) + cos(A−B).

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2θ = cos2θ − sin2θ = 2 cos2θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin2θ.

Complementary Angles

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

questions.question: What is the value of sin (90° + 2A)[4 - cos 2 (90° - 2A)]?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of sin (90° + 2A)[4 - cos2(90° - 2A)]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Substitute A = 0° in the expression: sin(90° + 0)[4 − cos2(90° − 0)] = 1 × [4 − 0] = 4.

Check Option (3): 4(cos6 0 + sin6 0) = 4(1 + 0) = 4.

Check Option (4): 4(cos6 0 − sin6 0) = 4(1 − 0) = 4.

Substitute A = 30°: Expression = cos 60°[4 − sin2 60°] = 0.5 × (4 − 0.75) = 1.625.

Check Option (4) for A = 30°: 4[(√3/2)6 − (1/2)6] = 4[27/64 − 1/64] = 26/16 = 1.625.

∴ The correct answer is 4(cos6A − sin6A).

Alternate Method

Given: sin(90° + 2A)[4 − cos2(90° − 2A)]

Formula Used: sin(90° + θ) = cos θ; cos(90° − θ) = sin θ; cos 2A = cos2 A − sin2 A; sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A; a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2)

⇒ sin(90° + 2A) = cos 2A

⇒ cos(90° − 2A) = sin 2A

⇒ Expression = cos 2A [4 − sin2 2A]

⇒ Substitute sin 2A = 2 sin A cos A: cos 2A [4 − (2 sin A cos A)2]

⇒ cos 2A [4 − 4 sin2 A cos2 A] = 4 cos 2A [1 − sin2 A cos2 A]

⇒ Substitute cos 2A = cos2 A − sin2 A and 1 = (cos2 A + sin2 A)2

⇒ 4 (cos2 A − sin2 A) [(cos2 A + sin2 A)2 − sin2 A cos2 A]

⇒ 4 (cos2 A − sin2 A) [cos4 A + sin4 A + 2 sin2 A cos2 A − sin2 A cos2 A]

⇒ 4 (cos2 A − sin2 A) [cos4 A + sin4 A + sin2 A cos2 A]

⇒ Since (x − y)(x2 + xy + y2) = x3 − y3, let x = cos2 A and y = sin2 A

⇒ Expression = 4 [(cos2 A)3 − (sin2 A)3] = 4 (cos6 A − sin6 A)

∴ The correct answer is 4(cos6A − sin6A).

Additional Information

Allied Angle Relations

Functions change at 90° and 270° (sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot) and signs depend on the quadrant.

Double Angle Identities

cos 2A = cos2 A − sin2 A = 2 cos2 A − 1 = 1 − 2 sin2 A.

Sum and Difference of Cubes

x3 − y3 = (x − y)(x2 + xy + y2) and x3 + y3 = (x + y)(x2 − xy + y2).

questions.question: What is the value of [cos(90° + A) ÷ sec (270° - A)] + [sin (270° + A) ÷ cosec (630° - A)]?
questions.questionHtml: What is the value of [cos(90° + A) ÷ sec (270° - A)] + [sin (270° + A) ÷ cosec (630° - A)]?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply ASTC (All-Silver-Tea-Cups) quadrant rules for each term.

cos(90° + A) = −sin A and sec(270° + A) → Here expression has sec(270° − A) = −cosec A.

sin(270° + A) = −cos A and cosec(630° − A) = cosec(360° + 270° − A) = cosec(270° − A) = −sec A.

Expression = [−sin A ÷ (−cosec A)] + [−cos A ÷ (−sec A)] = sin2A + cos2A = 1.

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Alternate Method

Given: [cos(90° + A) ÷ sec(270° − A)] + [sin(270° + A) ÷ cosec(630° − A)]

Formula Used: Quadrant transformations and sin2θ + cos2θ = 1.

⇒ Term 1: cos(90° + A) is in the 2nd quadrant. cos changes to sin and is negative.

⇒ cos(90° + A) = −sin A

⇒ Term 2: sec(270° − A) is in the 3rd quadrant. sec changes to cosec and is negative.

⇒ sec(270° − A) = −cosec A

⇒ Term 3: sin(270° + A) is in the 4th quadrant. sin changes to cos and is negative.

⇒ sin(270° + A) = −cos A

⇒ Term 4: cosec(630° − A) = cosec(360° + 270° − A) = cosec(270° − A)

⇒ 270° − A is in the 3rd quadrant. cosec changes to sec and is negative.

⇒ cosec(630° − A) = −sec A

⇒ Expression = [−sin A ÷ (−cosec A)] + [−cos A ÷ (−sec A)]

⇒ Expression = [sin A × sin A] + [cos A × cos A]

⇒ Expression = sin2A + cos2A

⇒ Expression = 1

∴ The correct answer is 1.

Additional Information

ASTC Rule

In the Cartesian plane, Trigonometric ratios are positive as follows: Q-I (All), Q-II (Sine/Cosec), Q-III (Tan/Cot), Q-IV (Cos/Sec).

Transformation at (n × 90° ± θ)

If n is odd, the ratio changes (sin↔cos, tan↔cot, sec↔cosec). If n is even, the ratio remains the same.

Trigonometric Identities

sin2θ + cos2θ = 1 | 1 + tan2θ = sec2θ | 1 + cot2θ = cosec2θ.

questions.question: On walking 100 metres towards a building in a horizontal line, the angle of elevation of its top changes from 45° to 60°. What will be the height (in metres) of the building?
questions.questionHtml: On walking 100 metres towards a building in a horizontal line, the angle of elevation of its top changes from 45° to 60°. What will be the height (in metres) of the building?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Use the direct distance formula: d = h(cot θ1 − cot θ2), where d is distance moved.

Here, d = 100 m, θ1 = 45° and θ2 = 60°.

100 = h(cot 45° − cot 60°) ⇒ 100 = h(1 − 1/√3).

100 = h(√3 − 1)/√3 ⇒ h = 100√3/(√3 − 1).

Rationalizing: h = [100√3 × (√3 + 1)] / 2 = 50(3 + √3).

∴ The correct answer is 50(3 + √3) m.

Alternate Method

Given: Initial angle θ1 = 45°, Final angle θ2 = 60°, Distance moved CD = 100 m.

Formula: tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

⇒ Let the height of the building AB be h and the initial distance BC be x.

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, tan 60° = AB / BC

⇒ √3 = h / x ⇒ x = h / √3 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ In right-angled ΔABD, tan 45° = AB / BD

⇒ 1 = h / (x + 100) ⇒ h = x + 100 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Substituting x from Eq 1 into Eq 2: h = (h / √3) + 100

⇒ h − h / √3 = 100 ⇒ h(1 − 1/√3) = 100

⇒ h(√3 − 1) / √3 = 100 ⇒ h = 100√3 / (√3 − 1)

⇒ Rationalizing the denominator: h = [100√3 × (√3 + 1)] / [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ h = [100(3 + √3)] / (3 − 1) ⇒ h = 100(3 + √3) / 2

⇒ h = 50(3 + √3) m.

∴ The correct answer is 50(3 + √3) m.

Additional Information

Distance-Height Relation

When moving towards an object, the relationship is h = d / (cot θ1 − cot θ2). If moving away, h = d / (cot θ2 − cot θ1).

Complementary Angles

If the angles of elevation from two points at distances 'a' and 'b' from the base are complementary, the height h = √(ab).

Standard Trig Ratios

tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3. Note that cot θ = 1/tan θ.

questions.question: Upper part of a tree broken over by the wind makes an angle of 60° with the ground. The distance between the root and the point where top of the tree touches the ground is 25 metres. What was the height (in metres) of the tree?
questions.questionHtml: Upper part of a tree broken over by the wind makes an angle of 60° with the ground. The distance between the root and the point where top of the tree touches the ground is 25 metres. What was the height (in metres) of the tree?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a broken tree forming angle θ with ground at distance d from the root:

Total Height = d × (tan θ + sec θ)

Given: d = 25 m and θ = 60°

Total Height = 25 × (tan 60° + sec 60°) = 25 × (√3 + 2)

Total Height = 25 × (1.732 + 2) = 25 × 3.732 = 93.3 m

∴ The correct answer is 93.3 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance from root to top on ground (BC) = 25 m

Angle of elevation (θ) = 60°

Formula Used:

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

cos θ = Base / Hypotenuse

Total height of tree = Vertical part (AB) + Broken part (AC)

In right-angled ΔABC:

⇒ tan 60° = AB / BC

⇒ √3 = AB / 25

⇒ AB = 25 × 1.732 = 43.3 m

⇒ cos 60° = BC / AC

⇒ 1/2 = 25 / AC

⇒ AC = 25 × 2 = 50 m

⇒ Total Height = AB + AC = 43.3 + 50 = 93.3 m

∴ The correct answer is 93.3 m.

Additional Information

Trigonometric Ratios in Broken Tree Problems

The height of the vertical standing part is found using tan θ = h/d, and the length of the fallen part (hypotenuse) is found using cos θ = d/l or sec θ = l/d.

Standard Values for √3 and √2

Commonly used approximations in competitive exams: √3 ≈ 1.732 and √2 ≈ 1.414.

Pythagoras Theorem Relation

For any such problem, the relation (Broken Part)2 = (Remaining Height)2 + (Distance from Root)2 always holds true.

questions.question: The height of a tower is 300 meters. When the top of another tower is seen from this tower, then the angle of depression is 60°. The horizontal distance between the bases of the two towers is 120 metres. What is the height (in metres) of the smaller tower?
questions.questionHtml: The height of a tower is 300 meters. When the top of another tower is seen from this tower, then the angle of depression is 60°. The horizontal distance between the bases of the two towers is 120 metres. What is the height (in metres) of the smaller tower?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Height of taller tower (H) = 300 m

Horizontal distance (d) = 120 m

Difference in height (Δh) = d × tan(60°) = 120 × √3

Δh = 120 × 1.732 = 207.84 m

Height of smaller tower (h) = H − Δh = 300 − 207.84 = 92.16 m

∴ The correct answer is 92.15 m.

Alternate Method

Given:

Height of taller tower (AB) = 300 m

Angle of depression = 60°

Horizontal distance (BD) = 120 m

Let the height of the smaller tower be CD = h.

From the diagram, the distance EC = BD = 120 m.

In ΔAEC, ∠ACE = 60° (Alternate interior angle to the angle of depression).

The height AE = AB − EB = 300 − h.

Using Trigonometric ratio in ΔAEC:

⇒ tan(60°) = AE / EC

⇒ √3 = (300 − h) / 120

⇒ 1.732 × 120 = 300 − h

⇒ 207.84 = 300 − h

⇒ h = 300 − 207.84

⇒ h = 92.16 m

Rounding to the nearest option provided:

∴ The correct answer is 92.15 m.

Additional Information

Angle of Depression

It is the angle formed between the horizontal line of sight and the line of sight to an object below the observer's eye level.

Trigonometric Values

Important values for Height & Distance: tan(30°) = 1/√3, tan(45°) = 1, and tan(60°) = √3.

Complementary Angles Rule

If the angle of elevation from the top of one tower to another is θ1 and the angle of depression is θ2, then the height difference is calculated using the respective tangents of these angles.

questions.question: In what ratio should tea costing Rs. 300/kg to be mixed with tea costing Rs. 200/kg so that the cost of the mixture is Rs. 225/kg?
questions.questionHtml: In what ratio should tea costing Rs. 300/kg to be mixed with tea costing Rs. 200/kg so that the cost of the mixture is Rs. 225/kg?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply the Alligation cross method:

Tea 1 (Dearer) = 300, Tea 2 (Cheaper) = 200, Mean Price = 225

Difference 1 (225 − 200) = 25

Difference 2 (300 − 225) = 75

Required Ratio = 25 : 75 = 1 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of Tea 1 = ₹300/kg

Cost of Tea 2 = ₹200/kg

Target Mixture Cost = ₹225/kg

Calculations:

⇒ Let the quantity of Tea 1 be x and Tea 2 be y.

⇒ According to Alligation rule, Ratio (x : y) = (Mean Price − Cost 2) : (Cost 1 − Mean Price)

⇒ Ratio = (225 − 200) : (300 − 225)

⇒ Ratio = 25 : 75

⇒ Ratio = 1 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 3.

Additional Information

Rule of Alligation

It is used to find the ratio in which two or more ingredients at their respective prices are mixed to produce a mixture of a specified price. Ratio = (Dearer Price − Mean Price) / (Mean Price − Cheaper Price).

Mean Price

The mean price is the cost price of a unit quantity of the mixture. It always lies between the cost price of the cheaper and dearer ingredients.

Replacement Formula

If x liters are removed from a container of C liters of pure liquid and replaced by water, after n operations, Quantity of pure liquid = C × (1 − x/C)n.
