questions.question: A is thrice as productive as C. Together they can complete a job in 22.5 days. If B joins them after they have worked for 15 days, then in how many days can they ﬁnish the rest of the job, while B alone can do the job in 15 days?
questions.questionHtml: A is thrice as productive as C. Together they can complete a job in 22.5 days. If B joins them after they have worked for 15 days, then in how many days can they ﬁnish the rest of the job, while B alone can do the job in 15 days?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Efficiency ratio A : C = 3 : 1 → Combined efficiency (A+C) = 4 units/day.

Total Work = (A+C) efficiency × Days = 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

B efficiency = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 units/day.

Remaining work after (A+C) work for 15 days = 90 − (4 × 15) = 30 units.

Days taken by (A+B+C) to finish = Remaining Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 30 ÷ (4 + 6) = 3 days.

∴ The correct answer is 3 days.

Alternate Method

Given: Efficiency of A = 3 × Efficiency of C. (A+C) time = 22.5 days. B's alone time = 15 days.

Formula Used: Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done.

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + C 22.5 90 units 90 ÷ 22.5 = 4
B 15 90 ÷ 15 = 6

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + C) = 4 units/day.

⇒ Total work = 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Work done by A and C in 15 days = 4 × 15 = 60 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 60 = 30 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency when B joins (A + B + C) = 4 + 6 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Time taken to finish remaining work = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 days.

∴ The correct answer is 3 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If efficiency ratio is x : y, then time ratio is y : x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person (Efficiency × Number of days worked).

Pipes and Cisterns

The same logic applies where efficiency is the rate of filling or emptying a tank per unit of time.

questions.question: If A, B and C can do a job working alone in 12, 18 and 36 days respectively. They all work together for 2 day, then B quits. How many days will A and C take to ﬁnish rest of the job?
questions.questionHtml: If A, B and C can do a job working alone in 12, 18 and 36 days respectively. They all work together for 2 day, then B quits. How many days will A and C take to ﬁnish rest of the job?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Work = LCM(12, 18, 36) = 36 units.

Efficiency: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1 (Combined = 6 units/day).

Work completed in 2 days = 6 × 2 = 12 units.

Remaining work = 36 − 12 = 24 units.

Time required for A and C = 24 ÷ (3 + 1) = 6 days.

∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time taken by A = 12 days

Time taken by B = 18 days

Time taken by C = 36 days

A, B, and C work together for 2 days, then B quits.

Method Used:

LCM Method for Time & Work

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 12 36 36 ÷ 12 = 3
B 18 36 ÷ 18 = 2
C 36 36 ÷ 36 = 1

Calculations:

⇒ Total efficiency of A, B, and C = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units/day

⇒ Total work done by all three in 2 days = 6 × 2 = 12 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done = 36 − 12 = 24 units

⇒ Efficiency of A and C together = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by A and C to finish remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 days

∴ The correct answer is 6 days.

Additional Information

Pipes & Cisterns

Similar to the Time & Work concept, inlet pipes have positive efficiency while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency. Total capacity is taken as the LCM of individual fill/empty times.

Work & Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If workers work for the same number of days, the wages are distributed directly in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Day Work

Calculate the combined work done in a complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people). Multiply the cycle to get close to the total work, then assign the remaining work sequentially to find the final time.

questions.question: If A, B and C together do a job in 4 days, A and C together do the job in 4.5 days and B and C together do the job in 12 days, then in how many days can C alone do the job?
questions.questionHtml: If A, B and C together do a job in 4 days, A and C together do the job in 4.5 days and B and C together do the job in 12 days, then in how many days can C alone do the job?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Total Work = LCM of (4, 4.5, 12) = 36 units.

Efficiency (A+B+C) = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 | Efficiency (A+C) = 36 ÷ 4.5 = 8 | Efficiency (B+C) = 36 ÷ 12 = 3.

Efficiency of B = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(A+C) = 9 − 8 = 1.

Efficiency of C = Eff(B+C) − Eff(B) = 3 − 1 = 2.

Time taken by C alone = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days.

∴ The correct answer is 18 days.

Alternate Method

Given:

Time (A+B+C) = 4 days

Time (A+C) = 4.5 days = 9/2 days

Time (B+C) = 12 days

Formula used: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A + B + C 4 36 9
A + C 4.5 8
B + C 12 3

⇒ Efficiency of (A+B+C) = 9 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of (A+C) = 8 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = (A+B+C) − (A+C) = 9 − 8 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Efficiency of (B+C) = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = (B+C) − B = 3 − 1 = 2 units/day

⇒ Days taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Days = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days

∴ The correct answer is 18 days.

Additional Information

Work and Efficiency Relation

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If time ratio is x:y, the efficiency ratio is y:x.

LCM Method for Fractions

LCM of fractions (a/b, c/d) = LCM(a, c) ÷ HCF(b, d). This is used to find total work when days are in fractions.

Combined Work Formula

If A does a job in x days and B in y days, together they do it in (x × y) ÷ (x + y) days.

questions.question: A alone can do a job in 40 days. In how many days can B alone do the job, if together they can do the job in 8 days?
questions.questionHtml: A alone can do a job in 40 days. In how many days can B alone do the job, if together they can do the job in 8 days?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When the time taken by person A and the time taken by (A + B) together are given, time for B is calculated as (Product of days) ÷ (Difference of days).

Time taken by B = (40 × 8) ÷ (40 − 8)

Time taken by B = 320 ÷ 32 = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Alternate Method

Given: A alone = 40 days, A + B together = 8 days.

Formula: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Person Days Total Work Efficiency
A 40 40 1
A + B 8 5

⇒ Total Work = LCM(40, 8) = 40 units

⇒ Efficiency of A = 40 ÷ 40 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Combined efficiency (A + B) = 40 ÷ 8 = 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = (Combined efficiency) − (Efficiency of A)

⇒ Efficiency of B = 5 − 1 = 4 units/day

⇒ Time taken by B = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of B = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 days

∴ The correct answer is 10 days.

Additional Information

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of efficiency is x:y, then the ratio of time taken is y:x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the work done by the individuals, which is same as the ratio of their efficiencies when they work for the same duration.

Combined Work for Three People

If three people A, B, and C can do a job in x, y, and z days respectively, then together they take (x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx) days.

questions.question: 1 bottle of honey costs Rs 240 but a pack of 4 of the same bottles costs Rs 768. What is the effective discount (in %) on the pack?
questions.questionHtml: 1 bottle of honey costs Rs 240 but a pack of 4 of the same bottles costs Rs 768. What is the effective discount (in %) on the pack?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total Marked Price (MP) for 4 bottles = 240 × 4 = ₹960.

Selling Price (SP) of the pack = ₹768.

Discount = MP − SP = 960 − 768 = ₹192.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (192 ÷ 960) × 100 = 20%.

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost of 1 bottle (Marked Price) = ₹240

Number of bottles in a pack = 4

Pack Selling Price = ₹768

Formula Used: Discount % = [(Marked Price − Selling Price) ÷ Marked Price] × 100

⇒ Total Marked Price of 4 bottles = 4 × 240 = ₹960 ⇒ Selling Price of the pack = ₹768 ⇒ Discount Amount = 960 − 768 = ₹192 ⇒ Discount % = (192 ÷ 960) × 100 ⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 ⇒ Discount % = 20%

∴ The correct answer is 20%.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are applied one after another, the equivalent discount is given by: a + b − (a × b ÷ 100).

Relation between CP, MP, and SP

Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 and CP = SP × 100 ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Buy X Get Y Free

In such offers, the discount percentage is calculated as: [Free Items (Y) ÷ Total Items (X + Y)] × 100.

questions.question: If the cost price of an article is Rs. x. It is marked up by 100%. It is sold at Rs. 1, 200 after giving 20% discount. What is value of x?
questions.questionHtml: If the cost price of an article is Rs. x. It is marked up by 100%. It is sold at Rs. 1, 200 after giving 20% discount. What is value of x?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Markup = 100% → Marked Price (MP) = 200% of CP.

Discount = 20% → Selling Price (SP) = 80% of MP.

Effective SP = 80% of 200% of CP = 160% of CP.

Given SP = 1200 ⇒ 160% = 1200.

Value of x (100%) = (1200 ÷ 160) × 100 = 7.5 × 100 = 750.

∴ The correct answer is ₹750.

Alternate Method

Given:

Cost Price (CP) = ₹x

Markup % = 100%

Discount % = 20%

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1200

Formula Used:

MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%)/100

Calculations:

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = x + (100% of x) = 2x

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − (20% of MP)

⇒ 1200 = 2x − (20 ÷ 100 × 2x)

⇒ 1200 = 2x − 0.4x

⇒ 1200 = 1.6x

⇒ x = 1200 ÷ 1.6

⇒ x = 750

∴ The correct answer is ₹750.

Additional Information

Markup and Discount Relation

The relationship between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by: CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%).

Effective Profit Percentage

Net Profit% = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount% ÷ 100). In this case: 100 − 20 − (100 × 20 ÷ 100) = 60% profit.

Successive Percentage Rule

If a value is increased by a% and then decreased by b%, the net change is [a − b − (ab/100)]%.

questions.question: A Rs. 1000 box of cookies is offered at 10% discount and a Rs. 400 bar of chocolate at 8% discount. If we buy 2 boxes of cookies and 3 bars of chocolate, what is the effective discount we get (in %)?
questions.questionHtml: A Rs. 1000 box of cookies is offered at 10% discount and a Rs. 400 bar of chocolate at 8% discount. If we buy 2 boxes of cookies and 3 bars of chocolate, what is the effective discount we get (in %)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total MP of Cookies = 2 × 1000 = ₹2000

Total MP of Chocolates = 3 × 400 = ₹1200

Ratio of Total MP = 2000 : 1200 = 5 : 3

Effective Discount % (Weighted Average) = (5 × 10% + 3 × 8%) ÷ (5 + 3)

Effective Discount % = (50 + 24) ÷ 8 = 74 ÷ 8 = 9.25%

∴ The correct answer is 9.25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

MP of 1 cookie box = ₹1000, Discount = 10%

MP of 1 chocolate bar = ₹400, Discount = 8%

Quantity: 2 cookie boxes and 3 chocolate bars

⇒ Total MP = (2 × 1000) + (3 × 400) = 2000 + 1200 = ₹3200

⇒ Discount on Cookies = 10% of 2000 = (10/100) × 2000 = ₹200

⇒ Discount on Chocolates = 8% of 1200 = (8/100) × 1200 = ₹96

⇒ Total Discount = 200 + 96 = ₹296

⇒ Effective Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total MP) × 100

⇒ Effective Discount % = (296 ÷ 3200) × 100 = 296 ÷ 32 = 9.25%

∴ The correct answer is 9.25%.

Additional Information

Effective Discount Formula

When buying multiple items with different discounts, the effective discount is (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d1% and d2% are given successively on a single item, the equivalent single discount is (d1 + d2 − d1×d2/100)%.

Relationship between MP, CP, and Profit

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). This is useful for finding the markup percentage.

questions.question: The price of a product after getting 20% discount is Rs. 3, 024 which includes 5% tax on selling price. What was the marked price (in Rs.) of the product?
questions.questionHtml: The price of a product after getting 20% discount is Rs. 3, 024 which includes 5% tax on selling price. What was the marked price (in Rs.) of the product?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Effective Multiplier = (1 − Discount%) × (1 + Tax%)

Effective Multiplier = 0.80 × 1.05 = 0.84

Marked Price (MP) = Final Price ÷ 0.84

MP = 3024 ÷ 0.84 = 3600

∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.

Alternate Method

Given:

Final Price (including tax) = ₹3,024

Discount = 20% on MP

Tax = 5% on Selling Price (SP)

Formula Used:

Final Price = SP + (Tax% of SP)

SP = MP − (Discount% of MP)

⇒ Final Price = SP × (1 + 5/100)

⇒ 3024 = SP × 1.05

⇒ SP = 3024 ÷ 1.05 = 2880

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − 20/100)

⇒ 2880 = MP × 0.80

⇒ MP = 2880 ÷ 0.80

⇒ MP = 3600

∴ The correct answer is ₹3600.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When multiple changes occur on a base value, the net change is calculated as Result = Base × (1 ± r1/100) × (1 ± r2/100).

Tax on Selling Price

Tax is always calculated on the net selling price (the price after all discounts have been applied) unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Marked Price is the label price, and Selling Price = Marked Price − Discount. The tax is then added to the Selling Price to get the total amount payable.

questions.question: If a dairy mixes cow’s milk which contains 10% fat with buffalo’s milk which contains 20% fat, then the resulting mixture has fat (120/7) % of fat. In what ratio was the cow’s milk mixed with buffalo’s milk?
questions.questionHtml:
If a dairy mixes cow’s milk which contains 10% fat with buffalo’s milk which contains
20% fat, then the resulting mixture has fat (120/7) % of fat. In what ratio was the
cow’s milk mixed with buffalo’s milk?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Apply Alligation Rule directly on fat percentages.

Cow Milk Fat = 10% | Buffalo Milk Fat = 20% | Mixture Fat = 120/7 %

Difference 1 (Buffalo − Mix) = 20 − 120/7 = 20/7

Difference 2 (Mix − Cow) = 120/7 − 10 = 50/7

Ratio (Cow : Buffalo) = 20/7 : 50/7 = 2 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Percentage of fat in Cow milk = 10%

Percentage of fat in Buffalo milk = 20%

Percentage of fat in the resulting mixture = 120/7 %

Formula used: Ratio of ingredients = (Higher Value − Mean Value) : (Mean Value − Lower Value)

⇒ Ratio of Cow milk to Buffalo milk = (20 − 120/7) : (120/7 − 10)

⇒ Ratio = [(140 − 120) / 7] : [(120 − 70) / 7]

⇒ Ratio = (20/7) : (50/7)

⇒ Ratio = 20 : 50

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 2 : 5.

Additional Information

Alligation Method

The rule of alligation states that when two ingredients are mixed, the ratio of the quantity of the cheaper to the quantity of the dearer is (CP of dearer − Mean Price) : (Mean Price − CP of cheaper).

Mean Value Constraint

The mean value or resulting percentage must always lie strictly between the values of the two individual components being mixed.

Weighted Average Formula

Alternatively, the mixture percentage can be calculated as M = (n1v1 + n2v2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the quantity and v is the value/concentration.

questions.question: The price of a movie ticket was increased in the ratio of 9 : 10. What is the increase in the revenue (in Rs.) of the cinema hall, if the original fare was Rs 180 and 2200 tickets were sold?
questions.questionHtml: The price of a movie ticket was increased in the ratio of 9 : 10. What is the increase in the revenue (in Rs.) of the cinema hall, if the original fare was Rs 180 and 2200 tickets were sold?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Price Ratio = 9 : 10

Original Price (9 units) = ₹180 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹20

Increase in Price = (10 − 9) = 1 unit = ₹20

Total Revenue Increase = Total Tickets × Increase per Ticket = 2200 × ₹20 = ₹44000

∴ The correct answer is ₹44000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Original fare (P1) = ₹180

Price Ratio (P1 : P2) = 9 : 10

Number of tickets sold (Q) = 2200

Formula Used:

Revenue = Price × Quantity

Increase in Revenue = (New Price − Original Price) × Quantity

Calculations:

⇒ Let the prices be 9x and 10x.

⇒ 9x = 180 ⇒ x = 20

⇒ New Price (10x) = 10 × 20 = ₹200

⇒ Increase in Price per ticket = 200 − 180 = ₹20

⇒ Total Revenue Increase = 2200 × 20

⇒ Total Revenue Increase = ₹44,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹44000.

Additional Information

Revenue and Expenditure Relationship

Total Revenue is the product of Price per unit and Quantity sold. If price increases by a ratio a:b and quantity remains constant, revenue also increases in the ratio a:b.

Net Effect Formula

If price changes by x% and quantity changes by y%, the net percentage change in revenue is given by: [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Ratio Method for Revenue Change

If Price ratio is P1:P2 and Quantity ratio is Q1:Q2, then Revenue ratio is (P1×Q1) : (P2×Q2).

questions.question: If 2A = 3B = 8C; What is A : B : C?
questions.questionHtml: If 2A = 3B = 8C; What is A : B : C?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Find the LCM of the coefficients of A, B, and C, which are 2, 3, and 8.

LCM(2, 3, 8) = 24.

Divide the LCM by each coefficient to get the ratio parts:

A = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 | B = 24 ÷ 3 = 8 | C = 24 ÷ 8 = 3.

∴ The correct answer is 12 : 8 : 3.

Alternate Method

Given: 2A = 3B = 8C

Let 2A = 3B = 8C = k

⇒ A = k/2

⇒ B = k/3

⇒ C = k/8

⇒ A : B : C = k/2 : k/3 : k/8

⇒ A : B : C = 1/2 : 1/3 : 1/8

⇒ To simplify, multiply by LCM of denominators (2, 3, 8) = 24

⇒ A : B : C = (24/2) : (24/3) : (24/8)

⇒ A : B : C = 12 : 8 : 3

∴ The correct answer is 12 : 8 : 3.

Additional Information

Reciprocal Ratio Property

If aX = bY = cZ, then the ratio X : Y : Z is equal to 1/a : 1/b : 1/c. This is essentially the inverse relationship between the coefficient and the variable.

Simplifying Ratios with Fractions

A ratio in fractional form (1/x : 1/y : 1/z) is converted to an integer ratio by multiplying all terms by the LCM of the denominators x, y, and z.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios (a : b) and (c : d), the compound ratio is defined as (ac : bd), which is the product of the antecedent and the product of the consequent.

questions.question: What is the number of candidates who had applied, if the ratio of selected to non-selected was 14 : 25? If 35 less had applied and 10 less had been selected, the ratio of selected to applied would have been 3 : 8.
questions.questionHtml: What is the number of candidates who had applied, if the ratio of selected to non-selected was 14 : 25? If 35 less had applied and 10 less had been selected, the ratio of selected to applied would have been 3 : 8.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Initial Ratio Selected (S) : Applied (A) = 14 : (14 + 25) = 14 : 39

New Ratio Selected (S) : Applied (A) = 3 : 8

Applying Cross-Multiplication Method:

(14 × 8 − 39 × 3) units = (3 × 35 − 8 × 10)

(112 − 117) units = 105 − 80 ⇒ 5 units = 25 ⇒ 1 unit = 5

Total Applied = 39 × 5 = 195

∴ The correct answer is 195 candidates.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Ratio (Selected : Non-selected) = 14 : 25

Applied candidates reduced by = 35

Selected candidates reduced by = 10

Final Ratio (Selected : Applied) = 3 : 8

Calculations:

Let Selected (S) = 14x and Non-selected (NS) = 25x

⇒ Total Applied (A) = S + NS = 14x + 25x = 39x

⇒ New Selected = 14x − 10

⇒ New Applied = 39x − 35

According to the condition:

⇒ (14x − 10) ÷ (39x − 35) = 3 ÷ 8

⇒ 8 × (14x − 10) = 3 × (39x − 35)

⇒ 112x − 80 = 117x − 105

⇒ 117x − 112x = 105 − 80

⇒ 5x = 25

⇒ x = 5

⇒ Initial Applied Candidates = 39x = 39 × 5 = 195

∴ The correct answer is 195 candidates.

Additional Information

Ratio Components

In ratio problems, the Total is always the sum of all parts. If Ratio A:B is m:n, then Total = (m + n)x.

Cross-Multiplication Method

Used to solve problems where a ratio changes after specific additions or subtractions: (Initial Ratio Product Diff) units = (Cross Product of Changes).

Proportionality Rule

If a : b = c : d, then product of extremes equals product of means (ad = bc).

questions.question: What is the fourth proportional to 6, 24 and 83?
questions.questionHtml: What is the fourth proportional to 6, 24 and 83?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Observe the ratio between the first two terms: 6 : 24 = 1 : 4.

The fourth proportional must maintain the same ratio with the third term.

Ratio 1 : 4 = 83 : x

x = 83 × 4 = 332.

∴ The correct answer is 332.

Alternate Method

Given:

First number (a) = 6

Second number (b) = 24

Third number (c) = 83

Formula Used:

If a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is the fourth proportional.

d = (b × c) ÷ a

Calculations:

⇒ Let the fourth proportional be x.

⇒ 6 : 24 :: 83 : x

⇒ 6 ÷ 24 = 83 ÷ x

⇒ 1 ÷ 4 = 83 ÷ x

⇒ x = 83 × 4

⇒ x = 332

∴ The correct answer is 332.

Additional Information

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Third Proportional

The third proportional to two numbers a and b is x such that a : b :: b : x, calculated as x = b2 ÷ a.

Product Property of Proportion

In any proportion a : b :: c : d, the product of the extremes (a × d) is always equal to the product of the means (b × c).

questions.question: Rs. 10,200 has to be divided between A, B & C so that A gets 2/3 of what B gets and B gets 1/4 of what C gets. How much more does C get over A (in Rs)?
questions.questionHtml: Rs. 10,200 has to be divided between A, B & C so that A gets 2/3 of what B gets and B gets 1/4 of what C gets. How much more does C get over A (in Rs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 1 : 4.

Combine ratios: A : B : C = 2 : 3 : (3 × 4) = 2 : 3 : 12.

Total units = 2 + 3 + 12 = 17 units.

17 units = ₹10,200 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹600.

Difference (C − A) = 12 − 2 = 10 units = 10 × 600 = ₹6000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total amount = ₹10,200

A = 2/3 B ⇒ A : B = 2 : 3

B = 1/4 C ⇒ B : C = 1 : 4

Formula Used:

Ratio Normalization: If A:B = x:y and B:C = p:q, then A:B:C = (x×p) : (y×p) : (y×q)

Calculations:

⇒ To equalize B, multiply A:B by 1 and B:C by 3

⇒ A : B = 2 : 3

⇒ B : C = 3 : 12

⇒ Combined Ratio A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 12

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 12 = 17

⇒ 17 units = 10,200

⇒ 1 unit = 10,200 ÷ 17 = 600

⇒ Share of C = 12 × 600 = ₹7,200

⇒ Share of A = 2 × 600 = ₹1,200

⇒ Difference = 7,200 − 1,200 = ₹6,000

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Additional Information

Ratio Balancing

When combining two ratios, ensure the common term has the same value by multiplying the ratios by appropriate constants.

Unitary Method in Ratios

Total Amount ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts gives the value of one ratio unit, which can then be multiplied by any part or difference.

Compound Ratio

A compound ratio is formed by multiplying the antecedents and consequents of two or more given ratios together.

questions.question: Before a battle, the ratio of captains to soldiers was 2 : 7. During the war 25 captains and 100 soldiers were martyred. The new ratio of captains to soldiers became 3 : 10. What is the number of soldiers after the war?
questions.questionHtml: Before a battle, the ratio of captains to soldiers was 2 : 7. During the war 25 captains and 100 soldiers were martyred. The new ratio of captains to soldiers became 3 : 10. What is the number of soldiers after the war?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Cross Multiplication Method for Ratios:

Initial Ratio = 2 : 7 | Final Ratio = 3 : 10 | Change = −25, −100

1 Unit = |(3 × 100) − (10 × 25)| ÷ |(2 × 10) − (3 × 7)|

1 Unit = |300 − 250| ÷ |20 − 21| = 50 ÷ 1 = 50

Initial Soldiers = 7 × 50 = 350

Soldiers after war = 350 − 100 = 250

∴ The correct answer is 250 soldiers.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial ratio (Captains : Soldiers) = 2 : 7

Martyred Captains = 25, Martyred Soldiers = 100

Final ratio (Captains : Soldiers) = 3 : 10

Calculations:

Let initial Captains be 2x and initial Soldiers be 7x.

⇒ (2x − 25) ÷ (7x − 100) = 3 ÷ 10

⇒ 10(2x − 25) = 3(7x − 100)

⇒ 20x − 250 = 21x − 300

⇒ 21x − 20x = 300 − 250

⇒ x = 50

⇒ Initial number of soldiers = 7x = 7 × 50 = 350

⇒ Number of soldiers after the war = 350 − 100 = 250

∴ The correct answer is 250 soldiers.

Additional Information

Cross-Product Rule for Ratios

When two ratios a:b and c:d change by specific values p and q, then 1 unit = |(c×q − d×p)| ÷ |(a×d − b×c)|.

Compound Ratio

The compound ratio of (a : b) and (c : d) is (ac : bd), obtained by multiplying corresponding terms.

Invertendo Property

If a : b = c : d, then b : a = d : c. This is useful for rearranging terms to solve for unknown variables.

questions.question: The average marks of 18 students in an examination were 60. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 63 instead of 36. The correct average is:
questions.questionHtml: The average marks of 18 students in an examination were 60. It was later found that the marks of one student had been wrongly entered as 63 instead of 36. The correct average is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Net change in marks = Correct value − Wrong value = 36 − 63 = −27

Average correction = Net change ÷ Number of students = −27 ÷ 18 = −1.5

New Average = Old Average + Average correction = 60 − 1.5 = 58.5

∴ The correct answer is 58.5.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number of students = 18

Incorrect average = 60

Wrong entry = 63

Correct entry = 36

Formula: Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of observations

⇒ Total incorrect marks = 18 × 60 = 1080

⇒ Total correct marks = 1080 − 63 + 36

⇒ Total correct marks = 1080 − 27 = 1053

⇒ Correct Average = 1053 ÷ 18

⇒ Correct Average = 58.5

∴ The correct answer is 58.5.

Additional Information

Average Correction Rule

Correct Average = Incorrect Average + [(Correct Value − Incorrect Value) ÷ Number of items].

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A1 and A2 and sizes n1 and n2 are combined, the new average is (n1A1 + n2A2) ÷ (n1 + n2).

Effect of Change

If every number in a dataset is increased/decreased by a constant 'k', the average also increases/decreases by exactly 'k'.

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, there are 20 girls who scored an average of 40 marks in the test. What is the average marks of the boys if the average of the class is 60 marks?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 60 students, there are 20 girls who scored an average of 40 marks in the test. What is the average marks of the boys if the average of the class is 60 marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Girls : Boys = 20 : 40 = 1 : 2

Class average (Mean) = 60 marks

Girls' average = 40 marks, which is 20 marks below the mean.

Total deficiency for 1 part of girls = 1 × −20 = −20

This deficiency must be balanced by 2 parts of boys: +20 ÷ 2 = +10 per boy part.

Average of boys = 60 + 10 = 70 marks.

∴ The correct answer is 70 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total students = 60

Average of class = 60 marks

Number of girls = 20

Average of girls = 40 marks

Formula Used:

Sum of values = Average × Number of entities

Average = Total Sum ÷ Total Number

⇒ Total marks of the class = 60 × 60 = 3600

⇒ Total marks scored by girls = 20 × 40 = 800

⇒ Number of boys = 60 − 20 = 40

⇒ Total marks scored by boys = Total marks − Girls marks

⇒ Total marks scored by boys = 3600 − 800 = 2800

⇒ Average marks of boys = 2800 ÷ 40

⇒ Average marks of boys = 70 marks

∴ The correct answer is 70 marks.

Additional Information

Weighted Average Formula

The average of a combined group is given by Acombined = (n1a1 + n2a2) ÷ (n1 + n2), where n is the count and a is the average.

Alligation Rule

The ratio of the quantities of two components is inversely proportional to the difference of their averages from the mean average: n1/n2 = (a2 − amean) / (amean − a1).

Deviation Method

Net deviation of all values from the arithmetic mean is always zero. This is useful for finding missing averages in combined groups.

questions.question: The average of 44 consecutive odd numbers is 144. What is the largest number?
questions.questionHtml: The average of 44 consecutive odd numbers is 144. What is the largest number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 187
Key Points
  • In a sequence of consecutive odd numbers or consecutive even numbers, the numbers form an Arithmetic Progression (AP) where the common difference is 2.
  • The Average of an Arithmetic Progression is always the middle term (if the number of terms is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if the number of terms is even).
  • For a set of n consecutive odd/even numbers, there is a direct shortcut formula to find the largest and smallest numbers if the average is known:
    Largest number = Average + (n − 1)
    Smallest number = Average − (n − 1)
  • Given in the question:
    Total numbers (n) = 44
    Average = 144
  • Applying the shortcut for the Largest number:
    Largest number = 144 + (44 − 1)
    Largest number = 144 + 43
    Largest number = 187
  • The logic holds because the average of 44 terms lies exactly between the 22nd and 23rd terms. Since the numbers are odd, and the average 144 is even, the 22nd term is 143 and the 23rd term is 145. To find the 44th term, we add 2 for every step moving forward from the average position.
Additional Information
  • To find the Smallest number in this series:
    Smallest number = Average − (n − 1)
    Smallest number = 144 − 43 = 101
  • Verification: The average of the first and last term of an AP is also the average of the whole series.
    Average = (101 + 187) ÷ 2
    Average = 288 ÷ 2 = 144. This confirms the calculation is correct.
  • The sum of n consecutive odd numbers can be calculated using the formula: Sum = Average × n. In this case, Sum = 144 × 44 = 6336.
  • The concept of Arithmetic Progression is vital for solving problems related to consecutive integers, multiples, and even/odd series efficiently.

questions.question: A batsman makes 100 runs in the 25 th match of his career. His average runs per match increases by 1.4. Find his average before the 25 th match.
questions.questionHtml: A batsman makes 100 runs in the 25<sup>th</sup> match of his career. His average runs per match increases by 1.4. Find his average before the 25<sup>th</sup> match.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total matches including the current one = 25

Total increase in runs across all matches = 25 × 1.4 = 35

Initial average (before 25th match) = Runs in 25th match − Total increase

Initial average = 100 − 35 = 65

∴ The correct answer is 65.

Alternate Method

Given: Runs in 25th match = 100, Increase in average = 1.4

Formula Used: Average = Total Runs ÷ Number of Matches

⇒ Let the average before the 25th match be x.

⇒ Total runs after 24 matches = 24 × x = 24x

⇒ Total runs after 25 matches = 24x + 100

⇒ New average = x + 1.4

⇒ Total runs after 25 matches = 25 × (x + 1.4)

⇒ 24x + 100 = 25x + 35

⇒ 25x − 24x = 100 − 35

⇒ x = 65

∴ The correct answer is 65.

Additional Information

Net Deviation Concept

The sum of deviations from the average is zero. If a new value is added, New Value = Old Average + (New Total Count × Increase in Average).

Average Calculation for Batsman

Batting Average = (Total Runs Scored) ÷ (Number of times Out). In standard problems, the number of matches is often used as the divisor.

Successive Changes in Average

When the average of n items is A, and one item is replaced by a new item of value x, the new average A' = A + (x − old value) ÷ n.

questions.question: An oil reﬁnery buys 10 barrels at Rs. 36000. There is 10% wastage. If the reﬁnery wants to earn 5% proﬁt then at what price should it sell including 8% tax on selling price? (in Rs. per barrel)
questions.questionHtml: An oil reﬁnery buys 10 barrels at Rs. 36000. There is 10% wastage. If the reﬁnery wants to earn 5% proﬁt then at what price should it sell including 8% tax on selling price? (in Rs. per barrel)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Usable quantity = 10 − 10% = 9 barrels.

Effective cost price per usable barrel = ₹36000 ÷ 9 = ₹4000.

Selling price with 5% profit = ₹4000 × 1.05 = ₹4200.

Final price with 8% tax = ₹4200 × 1.08 = ₹4536.

∴ The correct answer is ₹4536.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total cost of 10 barrels = ₹36000

Wastage = 10%

Desired Profit = 5%

Tax on Selling Price = 8%

Formula Used:

Final SP = [ (Total CP ÷ Usable Quantity) × (1 + Profit%) ] × (1 + Tax%)

Calculations:

⇒ Usable quantity = 10 barrels − (10% of 10) = 9 barrels

⇒ Cost Price per usable barrel = ₹36000 ÷ 9 = ₹4000

⇒ Target Profit = 5% of ₹4000 = (5 ÷ 100) × 4000 = ₹200

⇒ Base Selling Price (without tax) = ₹4000 + ₹200 = ₹4200

⇒ Tax amount = 8% of ₹4200 = (8 ÷ 100) × 4200 = ₹336

⇒ Final Selling Price (including tax) = ₹4200 + ₹336 = ₹4536

∴ The correct answer is ₹4536.

Additional Information

Wastage Impact on CP

When goods are wasted, the effective Cost Price per unit increases. Effective CP = Total CP ÷ (Initial Quantity − Wasted Quantity).

Tax on Selling Price

Tax is usually applied on the base selling price. Total SP = Base SP × (1 + Tax Rate/100).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value undergoes successive changes of x% and y%, the net effective change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: A vendor sells a coconut at Rs. 24 and suffers 24% loss. If he wants to make 14% proﬁt, then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.questionHtml: A vendor sells a coconut at Rs. 24 and suffers 24% loss. If he wants to make 14% proﬁt, then at what price (in Rs.) should he sell?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

In Profit and Loss, we treat CP as 100 units.

Loss of 24% → First SP = 100 − 24 = 76 units.

Profit of 14% → Required SP = 100 + 14 = 114 units.

Given: 76 units = Rs. 24

Required SP = (24 ÷ 76) × 114 = (6 ÷ 19) × 114 = 6 × 6 = 36.

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 36.

Alternate Method

Given:

Selling Price1 (SP1) = Rs. 24

Loss percentage = 24%

Desired Profit percentage = 14%

Formula Used:

Cost Price (CP) = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

New Selling Price (SP2) = [CP × (100 + Profit%)] ÷ 100

Calculations:

⇒ CP = (24 × 100) ÷ (100 − 24)

⇒ CP = 2400 ÷ 76 = Rs. 600/19

⇒ SP2 = [ (600/19) × (100 + 14) ] ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = [ (600/19) × 114 ] ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = (600 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SP2 = 3600 ÷ 100 = Rs. 36

∴ The correct answer is Rs. 36.

Additional Information

Direct Selling Price Relation

When CP is constant, SP1 / (100 ± x1%) = SP2 / (100 ± x2%), where x is the profit or loss percentage.

Marked Price and Discount

Selling Price can also be calculated using Marked Price (MP) and Discount%: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Profit and Loss on SP

Generally, profit/loss is calculated on CP. If the question specifies it is calculated on SP, then CP = SP − Profit or CP = SP + Loss.

questions.question: A villager buys a goat and a sheep together for Rs. 14,250. He sold the sheep at a proﬁt of 10% and the goat at a loss of 20%. If he sold both the animals at the same price, then what was the cost price of the cheaper animal?
questions.questionHtml: A villager buys a goat and a sheep together for Rs. 14,250. He sold the sheep at a proﬁt of 10% and the goat at a loss of 20%. If he sold both the animals at the same price, then what was the cost price of the cheaper animal?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

When Selling Price (SP) is same, the ratio of Cost Prices (CP1 : CP2) is the inverse of the Profit/Loss multipliers.

Ratio of CPSheep : CPGoat = 1/(100 + 10) : 1/(100 − 20) = 1/110 : 1/80 = 8 : 11

Total Ratio = 8 + 11 = 19 units → ₹14,250

1 unit = 14,250 ÷ 19 = ₹750

CP of cheaper animal (Sheep) = 8 units = 8 × 750 = ₹6000

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total CP of Sheep and Goat = ₹14,250

Profit on Sheep = 10% | Loss on Goat = 20%

Condition: SPSheep = SPGoat

Formula:

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (100 ± P/L)%

Calculations:

⇒ Let CP of Sheep be S and CP of Goat be G.

⇒ SP of Sheep = S × (110 / 100) = 1.1S

⇒ SP of Goat = G × (80 / 100) = 0.8G

⇒ Since SP is same: 1.1S = 0.8G

⇒ S / G = 0.8 / 1.1 = 8 / 11

⇒ Ratio S : G = 8 : 11

⇒ Total CP = 8x + 11x = 19x = 14250

⇒ x = 14250 ÷ 19 = 750

⇒ CP of Sheep (Cheaper) = 8 × 750 = ₹6000

⇒ CP of Goat (Costlier) = 11 × 750 = ₹8250

∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.

Additional Information

Same Selling Price Concept

If two items are sold at the same price, the ratio of their Cost Prices is given by CP1 : CP2 = (100 ± L2/P2) : (100 ± P1/L1).

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit % = (SP − CP)/CP × 100 and Loss % = (CP − SP)/CP × 100. All percentages are calculated on CP unless stated otherwise.

Overall Profit/Loss on Same SP

If two items are sold at the same SP, one at x% profit and another at x% loss, there is always an overall loss of (x/10)2 %.

questions.question: On a certain item proﬁt is 120%. If the cost price increases by 10% then what will be the new proﬁt margin (in %) if selling price remains the same?
questions.questionHtml: On a certain item proﬁt is 120%. If the cost price increases by 10% then what will be the new proﬁt margin (in %) if selling price remains the same?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume initial Cost Price (CP) = 100.

Profit = 120%, so Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 120 = 220.

New CP = 100 + 10% of 100 = 110.

Since SP remains same, New Profit = 220 − 110 = 110.

New Profit % = (110 ÷ 110) × 100 = 100%.

∴ The correct answer is 100%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Profit % = 120%

Increase in Cost Price (CP) = 10%

Selling Price (SP) = Constant

Formula Used:

SP = CP + Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let the initial CP be ₹100.

⇒ Initial Profit = 120% of ₹100 = ₹120.

⇒ SP = CP + Profit = 100 + 120 = ₹220.

⇒ New CP = Initial CP + 10% of CP = 100 + 10 = ₹110.

⇒ New Profit = SP − New CP = 220 − 110 = ₹110.

⇒ New Profit % = (New Profit ÷ New CP) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = (110 ÷ 110) × 100

⇒ New Profit % = 100%.

∴ The correct answer is 100%.

Additional Information

Profit and Loss on CP

Standard profit % or loss % is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless mentioned otherwise.

Effect of Change in CP

If CP increases while SP remains constant, the profit amount decreases and the profit percentage decreases more significantly because the base (CP) has increased.

Selling Price Formula

SP = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100 | SP = CP × (100 − Loss %)/100.

questions.question: In an exam, 35% are the passing marks. A student gets 200 marks yet fails by 24 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.questionHtml: In an exam, 35% are the passing marks. A student gets 200 marks yet fails by 24 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Passing Marks = Marks obtained + Marks failed by

Passing Marks = 200 + 24 = 224

Since 35% = 224 marks

Then 1% = 224 ÷ 35 = 6.4 marks

Maximum Marks (100%) = 6.4 × 100 = 640 marks

∴ The correct answer is 640 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

Passing Percentage = 35%

Marks Obtained = 200

Failing Margin = 24 marks

Formula Used:

Passing Marks = (Passing Percentage / 100) × Maximum Marks

⇒ Let the Maximum Marks be x.

⇒ Passing Marks = Marks Obtained + Fail Margin

⇒ Passing Marks = 200 + 24 = 224

⇒ 35% of x = 224

⇒ (35/100) × x = 224

⇒ x = (224 × 100) / 35

⇒ x = (32 × 100) / 5

⇒ x = 32 × 20

⇒ x = 640

∴ The correct answer is 640 marks.

Additional Information

Passing Marks and Percentage

The minimum marks required to pass is always calculated as: Passing Marks = (Passing Percentage × Maximum Marks) ÷ 100.

Finding Maximum Marks from Two Students

If student A fails by 'a' marks and student B gets 'b' marks more than passing marks, then Max Marks = (Difference in Marks ÷ Difference in Percentage) × 100.

Percentage Increase/Decrease

To find the percentage change between two values: % Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

questions.question: A student gets 22 marks more in French than what she got in German. Her German marks are 28% of the sum of her French and German marks. What are her French marks?
questions.questionHtml: A student gets 22 marks more in French than what she got in German. Her German marks are 28% of the sum of her French and German marks. What are her French marks?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Total Marks (French + German) = 100%

German Marks = 28%, so French Marks = 100% − 28% = 72%

Difference in Percentage = 72% − 28% = 44%

Given Difference = 22 marks → 44% = 22 → 1% = 0.5 marks

French Marks = 72% = 72 × 0.5 = 36 marks

∴ The correct answer is 36 marks.

Alternate Method

Given:

French marks (F) − German marks (G) = 22

German marks (G) = 28% of (F + G)

Formula:

Value = (Percentage / 100) × Total Sum

⇒ Let French marks be F and German marks be G.

⇒ G = 0.28 × (F + G)

⇒ G = 0.28F + 0.28G

⇒ G − 0.28G = 0.28F

⇒ 0.72G = 0.28F

⇒ G = (28 / 72) × F = (7 / 18) × F

⇒ Given: F − G = 22

⇒ F − (7 / 18)F = 22

⇒ (11 / 18)F = 22

⇒ F = (22 × 18) / 11

⇒ F = 2 × 18 = 36

∴ The correct answer is 36 marks.

Additional Information

Percentage Base Change

When comparing two quantities, the difference remains constant but the percentage varies based on which quantity is taken as the denominator (base).

Successive Percentage

If a value changes by x% and then by y%, the net change is given by [x + y + (xy / 100)]%.

Relative Value calculation

If A is k% more than B, then B is [k / (100 + k)] × 100% less than A.

questions.question: 2% of a = b, then b% of 10 is the same as:
questions.questionHtml: 2% of a = b, then b% of 10 is the same as:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Given: b = 2% of a ⇒ b = 0.02a

Required: b% of 10 = (b ÷ 100) × 10 = b ÷ 10

Substitute b: (0.02a) ÷ 10 = 0.002a

Check Option (2): 20% of a/100 = (20 ÷ 100) × (a ÷ 100) = 0.2 × 0.01a = 0.002a

∴ The correct answer is 20% of a/100.

Alternate Method

Given: 2% of a = b

Formula Used: x% of y = (x × y) ÷ 100

⇒ b = (2 ÷ 100) × a

⇒ b = 2a ÷ 100

⇒ Required value = b% of 10 = (b ÷ 100) × 10

⇒ Required value = (b × 10) ÷ 100 = b ÷ 10

⇒ Substituting the value of b: (2a ÷ 100) ÷ 10 = 2a ÷ 1000

⇒ Checking Option (2): 20% of a/100 = (20 ÷ 100) × (a ÷ 100) = 20a ÷ 10000 = 2a ÷ 1000

⇒ Since both expressions result in 2a/1000, Option (2) is correct.

∴ The correct answer is 20% of a/100.

Additional Information

Commutative Property of Percentages

x% of y is always equal to y% of x. Formula: (x × y) ÷ 100 = (y × x) ÷ 100.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert a percentage into a fraction, divide by 100. Example: 2% = 2/100 = 1/50.

Successive Percentages

a% of b% of c = (a × b × c) ÷ 10000. This is useful for multi-step percentage problems.

questions.question: A man’s annual income has increased by Rs. 1.2 lakhs but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 12% to 10%. He now pays the same amount of tax as before. What is his increased income (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.questionHtml: A man’s annual income has increased by Rs. 1.2 lakhs but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 12% to 10%. He now pays the same amount of tax as before. What is his increased income (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Tax Rates = 12% : 10% = 6 : 5.

As Tax Amount is constant, Income is inversely proportional to Tax Rate.

Income Ratio = 5 : 6.

Increase in ratio = 6 − 5 = 1 unit = 1.2 lakhs.

Increased Income = 6 units = 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is 7.2 lakhs.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial tax rate = 12%

New tax rate = 10%

Income increase = ₹ 1.2 lakhs

Tax paid before = Tax paid after

Let the initial income be x lakhs.

Increased income = (x + 1.2) lakhs.

⇒ Tax paid initially = 12% of x = 0.12x

⇒ Tax paid now = 10% of (x + 1.2) = 0.10(x + 1.2)

Since the tax amount is the same:

⇒ 0.12x = 0.10(x + 1.2)

⇒ 12x = 10(x + 1.2)

⇒ 12x = 10x + 12

⇒ 12x − 10x = 12

⇒ 2x = 12

⇒ x = 6 lakhs

Increased income = x + 1.2 = 6 + 1.2 = 7.2 lakhs.

∴ The correct answer is 7.2 lakhs.

Additional Information

Inverse Variation Rule

When the product of two variables is constant (Income × Tax Rate = Total Tax), then the variables are inversely proportional to each other. If the rate decreases by a certain ratio, the income must increase by the reciprocal ratio to keep the tax same.

Percentage Change Logic

If a value is reduced by r%, to restore it to the original value, it must be increased by [r / (100 − r)] × 100%.

Taxable Income

Net Income = Gross Income − Income Tax. In this problem, we dealt with the gross income and the tax rates applied to it.

questions.question: A car travelling at an average speed of 72 km/hr takes 9 minutes to travel a certain distance. By how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to travel the same distance in 8 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: A car travelling at an average speed of 72 km/hr takes 9 minutes to travel a certain distance. By how much should it increase its speed (in km/hr) to travel the same distance in 8 minutes?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

For a constant distance, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T).

Ratio of Time = 9 : 8

Ratio of Speed = 8 : 9

Initial Speed (8 units) = 72 km/hr ⇒ 1 unit = 9 km/hr

Increase in speed = 9 − 8 = 1 unit = 9 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Initial Speed (S1) = 72 km/hr

Initial Time (T1) = 9 minutes = 9/60 hours

New Time (T2) = 8 minutes = 8/60 hours

Formula: Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = S1 × T1

⇒ Distance = 72 × (9/60) = 10.8 km

⇒ New Speed (S2) = Distance ÷ T2

⇒ S2 = 10.8 ÷ (8/60) = (10.8 × 60) ÷ 8

⇒ S2 = 648 ÷ 8 = 81 km/hr

⇒ Increase in speed = S2 − S1

⇒ Increase in speed = 81 − 72 = 9 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.

Additional Information

Relationship between Speed, Distance, and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S1 × T1 = S2 × T2). If distance varies, then Distance ∝ Speed × Time.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

questions.question: Train A takes 1 hour more than train B to travel a distance of 720 km. Due to engine trouble speed of train B falls by one third, so it takes 3 hours more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?
questions.questionHtml: Train A takes 1 hour more than train B to travel a distance of 720 km. Due to engine trouble speed of train B falls by one third, so it takes 3 hours more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed ratio for Train B = 1 : (1 − 1/3) = 1 : 2/3 = 3 : 2

Time ratio for Train B = 2 : 3 (Inverse of speed ratio as distance is constant)

Difference in B's time = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Actual time difference for B = (Time A + 3) − (Time A − 1) = 4 hours

∴ 1 unit = 4 hours → Original time of B = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

Time taken by Train A = 8 + 1 = 9 hours → Speed A = 720 ÷ 9 = 80 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given: Distance = 720 km. Train A time = Train B time + 1 hr. After speed reduction of 1/3, New Train B time = Train A time + 3 hr.

Formula Used: Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed ∝ 1/Time (when distance is constant)

Let original speed and time of Train B be Sb and Tb respectively.

⇒ Ta = Tb + 1 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ New Speed of B = Sb − (1/3)Sb = 2/3 Sb

⇒ New Time of B (Tb') = Distance ÷ (2/3 Sb) = 3/2 (Distance ÷ Sb) = 3/2 Tb

⇒ Tb' = Ta + 3 --- (Eq. 2)

Substitute Ta from Eq. 1 into Eq. 2:

⇒ 3/2 Tb = (Tb + 1) + 3

⇒ 3/2 Tb − Tb = 4

⇒ 1/2 Tb = 4

⇒ Tb = 8 hours

⇒ Ta = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

⇒ Speed of Train A = Distance ÷ Ta = 720 ÷ 9

⇒ Speed of Train A = 80 km/hr

∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.

Additional Information

Inverse Relationship of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S1/S2 = T2/T1). This allows solving complex speed problems using simple ratios.

Average Speed Formula

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. For two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x + y).

Unit Conversions

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Two cars A and B travel from one city to another city, at speeds of 60 km/hr and 108 km/hr respectively. If car B takes 2 hours lesser time than car A for the journey, then what is the distance (in km) between the two cities?
questions.questionHtml: Two cars A and B travel from one city to another city, at speeds of 60 km/hr and 108 km/hr respectively. If car B takes 2 hours lesser time than car A for the journey, then what is the distance (in km) between the two cities?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Distance = (Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds) × Time Difference

D = (60 × 108 ÷ (108 − 60)) × 2

D = (6480 ÷ 48) × 2

D = 135 × 2 = 270 km

∴ The correct answer is 270 km.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed of Car A (SA) = 60 km/hr

Speed of Car B (SB) = 108 km/hr

Time difference (Δt) = 2 hours

Ratio Method:

⇒ Speed Ratio (A : B) = 60 : 108

⇒ Speed Ratio (A : B) = 5 : 9

⇒ Since Distance is constant, Time Ratio ∝ 1/Speed Ratio

⇒ Time Ratio (A : B) = 9 : 5

⇒ Difference in time parts = 9 − 5 = 4 units

⇒ 4 units = 2 hours

⇒ 1 unit = 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5 hours

⇒ Total time taken by Car A = 9 units = 9 × 0.5 = 4.5 hours

⇒ Distance = Speed of A × Time of A

⇒ Distance = 60 × 4.5

⇒ Distance = 270 km

∴ The correct answer is 270 km.

Additional Information

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S1/S2 = T2/T1).

Distance Formula for Time Difference

Distance = [ (S1 × S2) / |S1 − S2| ] × Total Time Difference (ΔT).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: B starts 4.5 minutes after A from the same point, for a place at a distance of 3.5 miles from the starting point. A on reaching the destination turns back and walks a mile where he meets B. If A’s speed is a mile in 6 minutes, then B’s speed is a mile in _______ minutes.
questions.questionHtml: B starts 4.5 minutes after A from the same point, for a place at a distance of 3.5 miles from the starting point. A on reaching the destination turns back and walks a mile where he meets B. If A’s speed is a mile in 6 minutes, then B’s speed is a mile in _______ minutes.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Total distance covered by A = 3.5 + 1 = 4.5 miles.

Total time taken by A = 4.5 × 6 = 27 minutes.

Time taken by B = 27 − 4.5 = 22.5 minutes.

Distance covered by B = 3.5 − 1 = 2.5 miles.

B’s speed (minutes per mile) = 22.5 ÷ 2.5 = 9 minutes.

∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.

Alternate Method

Given:

Total distance to destination = 3.5 miles

A's speed = 1 mile in 6 minutes

B starts = 4.5 minutes after A

Meeting point = 1 mile before the destination

Formula Used:

Time = Distance × (Minutes per mile)

Pace (Minutes per mile) = Total Time ÷ Total Distance

Calculations:

⇒ Distance covered by A = 3.5 (to destination) + 1 (return) = 4.5 miles

⇒ Time taken by A = 4.5 miles × 6 minutes/mile = 27 minutes

⇒ Since B starts 4.5 minutes later and meets A at that moment,

⇒ Time taken by B = Time of A − Delay = 27 − 4.5 = 22.5 minutes

⇒ Distance covered by B = Total distance − Distance A walked back

⇒ Distance covered by B = 3.5 − 1 = 2.5 miles

⇒ B’s pace = Time ÷ Distance = 22.5 ÷ 2.5

⇒ B’s pace = 9 minutes per mile

∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.

Additional Information

Meeting Point Logic

When two people travel towards each other, the time of meeting is the same for both relative to their individual start times, adjusted for any delay.

Speed and Time Relation

Pace is the reciprocal of speed. If speed is S miles/min, then pace is 1/S min/mile. Time = Distance × Pace.

Relative Speed

In this scenario, after A turns back, A and B are moving toward each other. The sum of their distances covered from that moment equals the remaining distance between them.

questions.question: If the compound interest received on a certain amount in the 3 rd year is Rs. 12,100, what will be the compound interest (in Rs.) for the 4 th year on the same amount, if rate of interest is 9%?
questions.questionHtml: If the compound interest received on a certain amount in the 3<sup>rd</sup> year is Rs. 12,100, what will be the compound interest (in Rs.) for the 4<sup>th</sup> year on the same amount, if rate of interest is 9%?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Compound interest for any year is (100 + R)% of the interest of the previous year.

Interest for 4th year = Interest for 3rd year × (100 + 9)%

Interest for 4th year = 12100 × 1.09 = 13189.

∴ The correct answer is ₹13189.

Alternate Method

Given:

Compound interest for 3rd year = ₹12,100

Rate of interest (R) = 9% per annum

Formula Used:

CI(n+1)th year = CInth year + (CInth year × R ÷ 100)

Calculations:

⇒ Interest on 3rd year CI = 12100 × 9 ÷ 100

⇒ Interest on 3rd year CI = 121 × 9

⇒ Interest on 3rd year CI = 1089

⇒ 4th year CI = 3rd year CI + Interest on 3rd year CI

⇒ 4th year CI = 12100 + 1089

⇒ 4th year CI = 13189

∴ The correct answer is ₹13189.

Additional Information

Consecutive Year Interest Relation

The compound interest for the (n+1)th year is equal to the compound interest of the nth year plus the interest calculated on that amount for one year: CIn+1 = CIn × (1 + R/100).

Difference between SI and CI for 2 years

The difference between Simple Interest and Compound Interest for a period of 2 years on Principal P at Rate R% is given by D = P × (R ÷ 100)2.

Effective Interest Rate

For two successive years with interest rate R%, the effective compound interest rate over the two-year period is (R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: The amount received at 10% per annum compound interest after 3 yrs is Rs. 10,648. What was the principal (in Rs.)?
questions.questionHtml: The amount received at 10% per annum compound interest after 3 yrs is Rs. 10,648. What was the principal (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Rate of interest = 10% = 1/10.

For Compound Interest, the ratio of Principal (P) to Amount (A) for 1 year is 10 : 11.

For 3 years, the ratio P : A = 103 : 113 = 1000 : 1331.

Given Amount = 1331 units = ₹10,648.

1 unit = 10,648 ÷ 1331 = 8.

Principal = 1000 units = 1000 × 8 = ₹8000.

∴ The correct answer is ₹8000.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount (A) = ₹10,648

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Time (n) = 3 years

Formula Used:

A = P(1 + R/100)n

Calculations:

⇒ 10,648 = P(1 + 10/100)3

⇒ 10,648 = P(1 + 1/10)3

⇒ 10,648 = P(11/10)3

⇒ 10,648 = P × (1331 / 1000)

⇒ P = (10,648 × 1000) / 1331

⇒ P = 8 × 1000

⇒ P = ₹8000

∴ The correct answer is ₹8000.

Additional Information

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate R, the effective CI rate for 3 years is [ (1 + R/100)3 − 1 ] × 100%. For 10%, it is 33.1%.

Difference between CI and SI

For 3 years: Difference = P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100). For 2 years: Difference = P(R/100)2.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate is halved (R/2) and the time period is doubled (2n).

questions.question: In how many years will Rs. 25,000 yield Rs. 8,275 as compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually?
questions.questionHtml: In how many years will Rs. 25,000 yield Rs. 8,275 as compound interest at 10% per annum compounded annually?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of Amount (A) to Principal (P) = (25,000 + 8,275) : 25,000 = 33,275 : 25,000

Simplifying the ratio: 1,331 : 1,000

Expressing as powers: (11)3 : (10)3 = (11/10)3

Since Rate = 10% = 1/10, the annual multiplier is (1 + 1/10) = 11/10

The power 3 directly represents the number of years.

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Principal (P) = ₹25,000

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹8,275

Rate (R) = 10% per annum

Formula Used:

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)n, where n is the time in years.

⇒ Amount = Principal + CI

⇒ A = 25,000 + 8,275 = 33,275

⇒ 33,275 = 25,000 × (1 + 10/100)n

⇒ 33,275 / 25,000 = (11/10)n

⇒ 13,31 / 10,00 = (11/10)n

⇒ (11/10)3 = (11/10)n

⇒ n = 3

∴ The correct answer is 3 years.

Additional Information

Compound Interest Formula

CI = P[(1 + R/100)n − 1]. Interest is calculated on the principal and the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a 10% annual rate compounded annually for 3 years, the effective rate is 33.1%. (25,000 × 33.1% = 8,275).

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference is P(R/100)2. For 3 years, the difference is P(R/100)2 × (3 + R/100).

questions.question: What is the rate of interest, if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3 rd year is Rs. 1,750 and compound interest earned for 2 years is Rs. 3622.5?
questions.questionHtml: What is the rate of interest, if simple interest earned on a certain sum for the 3<sup>rd</sup> year is Rs. 1,750 and compound interest earned for 2 years is Rs. 3622.5?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Simple Interest (SI) is constant every year → SI for 1st year = SI for 3rd year = ₹1,750.

Total SI for 2 years = 1,750 × 2 = ₹3,500.

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years (D) = ₹3,622.5 − ₹3,500 = ₹122.5.

Rate of Interest (R) = (Difference ÷ SI of 1st year) × 100.

R = (122.5 ÷ 1,750) × 100 = 7%.

∴ The correct answer is 7%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Simple interest for 3rd year = ₹1,750

Compound interest for 2 years = ₹3,622.5

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 1 year = SI for 3rd year = ₹1,750

⇒ Total SI for 2 years = 1,750 × 2 = ₹3,500

⇒ Difference (D) = CI2 years − SI2 years

⇒ D = 3,622.5 − 3,500 = ₹122.5

⇒ This difference is the interest calculated on the first year's SI.

⇒ Rate (R) = (D × 100) ÷ (SI for 1 year)

⇒ R = (122.5 × 100) ÷ 1,750

⇒ R = 12,250 ÷ 1,750 = 7%

∴ The correct answer is 7%.

Additional Information

Relationship between CI and SI for 2 years

The ratio of Compound Interest to Simple Interest for 2 years is given by CI/SI = (1 + R/200).

Difference Formula for 2 Years

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years is D = P(R/100)2, where P is the Principal and R is the rate.

Successive Percentage Rule

Effective CI rate for 2 years can be calculated as R + R + (R × R)/100.
